messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@lumina.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High tail latency 2026-12-10 to 12 — SLA relief request

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Quick note from Lumina ops: between 2026-12-10 03:20 UTC and 2026-12-12 18:05 UTC we observed elevated tail latency on your hosted inference endpoints (model: redwood-llama-ggml-v1). This impacted synchronous inference for a subset (~12%) of our production traffic and caused request timeouts inside our user flows. We opened a ticket (OPS-1432) and worked with your on-call but the window materially affected our peak hours.

Per section 4.2 of our SOW (SLA: 99.95% monthly uptime), we would like to discuss a remediation package—either a prorated invoice credit for the impacted period or a short-term service credit/discount while you complete root cause mitigation. For planning purposes, please propose 1) a concrete dollar credit option and 2) a temporary uplift in capacity (burst) for our Dedicated pool for the next 30 days to avoid recurrence.

Attached is our internal incident timeline and sample request traces. We appreciate a prompt proposal; our procurement team needs an estimate by COB Friday to include in the month-end reconciliation.

Thanks,
Jordan Ellis\Director of Platform Reliability\Lumina AI

Attachments: incident-summary-lumina-2026-12.pdf, usage-report-202612.csv

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Marissa / Jonas / Karthik,

Forwarding Lumina's ask. Quick context: Lumina is a mid-enterprise customer running a Dedicated pool (SOW-0045). They hit increased p95/p99 latency during a model rollout we staged on 12/10; engineering throttled rollout but the KV cache warmup and a kernel mismatch caused higher latency on long-sequence requests.

Lumina wants a dollar estimate for credit + a short-term Dedicated burst. They asked for a reply by Friday COB. Marissa, can you draft a proposed concession (numbers + rationale) we can present to Karthik for exec sign-off? Jonas, can you confirm the burst availability and cost impact for the next 30 days (regions: us-west-2)?

I'll attach the customer's incident packet they sent.

— Soojin

Redwood Inference

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed remediation package for Lumina — numbers and rationale

Karthik / Jonas,

Below is a concise proposal to resolve Lumina's ask and keep the renewal on-track. I'm including the minimal background and an attachment with the usage export and SOW excerpt.

Summary of impact
- Impact window: 2026-12-10 03:20 UTC — 2026-12-12 18:05 UTC
- Estimated affected billable tokens: ~14.2M (customer-supplied usage export; see attachment)
- December invoice (projected): $182,500

Proposed remediation package (options for exec selection)
A) One-time invoice credit: 20% of December invoice (~$36,500) + a technical remediation report and 2 weeks of Dedicated burst (no charge) to stabilize rollout.
B) Tiered credit: prorated credit equal to (estimated affected tokens / total monthly tokens) * invoice * 1.5 multiplier (expected ~ $28k) + 30-day burst at cost.
C) One-time fixed cap: $25,000 credit + one free month of Redwood Optimize add-on at no charge.

Recommendation: Offer option A but cap at $35k to keep precedent conservative. Add a customer success commitment: a joint postmortem and a bi-weekly monitoring window for 6 weeks. This balances making Lumina whole without setting an outsized precedent.

Attachments: usage-report-202612.csv; SOW-0045-service-terms.pdf; incident-summary-lumina-2026-12.pdf

If you approve option A (cap $35k) I will send the offer to Lumina with clear terms and logging as a one-off ex gratia concession.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Enterprise AE, Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed remediation package for Lumina — numbers and rationale

Thanks for the clear options, Marissa. I agree with the balanced approach. Approve option A with two adjustments:

1) Cap the one-time credit at $35,000 (rounded).
2) In lieu of a 30-day unmanaged burst, commit to a targeted Dedicated burst for Lumina for the next 30 days limited to 2x their current reserved capacity; engineering will schedule this and provide a daily short report. This reduces operational risk and shows good faith.

Operational items — please do the following before sending to Lumina:
- Include a one-paragraph description of the mitigation actions we took and a 2-week monitoring cadence.
- State explicitly this is a one-time ex gratia concession; no contract amendment or precedent for future incidents.
- CC Legal if Lumina requests contract language.

Approving for exec sign-off.

— Karthik
VP Sales Operations (interim)
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@lumina.ai>, Lumina AI Billing <billing@lumina.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 17:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High tail latency 2026-12-10 to 12 — remediation offer

Hi Jordan — thanks for your patience while we reviewed this internally. We appreciate the timelines you shared and the traces; apologies again for the disruption.

Redwood proposal (approved by our leadership):
- One-time invoice credit equal to 20% of your December invoice, capped at $35,000 (we will apply the credit to the invoice generated in January).
- A Dedicated capacity burst for Lumina for 30 days (us-west-2) limited to 2x your current reserved capacity; engineering will stand up the burst and provide daily status notes for the first week and then weekly thereafter for the remainder.
- A joint remediation report summarizing root cause analysis and actions we took; a 2-week monitoring cadence with Customer Success to verify stability.

This concession is provided as a one-time ex gratia remediation and does not change the SOW or create a contractual amendment. If Lumina would prefer a different structure (for example a fixed cash credit in lieu of the cap formula) let me know and we can evaluate.

Next steps
1) Please confirm acceptance of the offer and the preferred point-of-contact for scheduling the Dedicated burst.
2) If accepted, our billing operations will issue a credit memo against January's invoice and engineering will start the burst provisioning within 24 hours of acceptance.

Best,
Soojin Lee\Account Lead — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
